paper_title: Search of spin-dependent fifth forces with precision magnetometry
suggested_experiment_name: SQUID magnetometry spin-mass (Crescini et al. This work)
coupling_convention: g_p^e g_s^N, dimensionless product of pseudoscalar-electron and scalar-nucleon couplings, as plotted
notes: SQUID-magnetometer spin-mass fifth force search. The paper reports g_p^e g_s^N <= 5.7e-32 for lambda >~ 10 cm (electron-nucleon monopole-dipole), and g_p^e g_s^e <= 1.6e-31 for electron-electron. Text gives flat-ish bounds valid over ranges 1cm-10m and 10km-300km; the exact mass-dependent curve is in Fig.4 (not numerically tabulated). Encoded the electron-nucleon limit as a horizontal line spanning roughly the mass range shown on the axis (approx 0.002 to 20 ueV -> ~2e-9 to ~2e-5 eV). Masses given are approximate from lambda = h/mc for cm-to-hundreds-of-km ranges; used representative span. Convention g_p^e g_s^N matches MonopoleDipole g_s*g_p product. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.72, 33)) | Vision: Traced the blue 'This work' (SQUID and paramagnets) lower boundary from Fig.4 upper panel. X-axis converted from lambda[m] to mass[eV] via m=1.240e-6/lambda (Compton wavelength), consistent with the top m[mueV] axis. Text confirms best limit g_p^e g_s^N <= 5.7e-32 for lambda >~ 10 cm (m <~ 1.24e-5 eV). The flat plateau of the excluded boundary is at ~5.7e-32 across the long-lambda (low-mass) region, rising steeply at short lambda (high mass). Note plot y-axis quantity is the product g_p^e g_s^N. | Calibration: No calibration needed (spot-check verify/stage2 raw_ratio=1.75 snapped to identity)
